sources.title: Kansas Statutes 44-717 (collection of employer payments; penalties and interest on past-due reports and payments; electronic filing of wage reports, contribution returns and payments)
sources.revision: K.S.A. 44-717 as published by the Kansas Revisor of Statutes (history through L. 2024, ch. 83, section 9)
sources.verifiedBy: fetched and read in full on 2026-11-12: (a)(1) an employer that fails to file a wage report or contribution return by the last day of the month following the close of the calendar quarter pays a penalty of .05% of the total wages paid in the quarter for each month or fraction of a month until it is received, never less than $25 nor more than $200 per report; contributions unpaid by the last day of the month following the quarter bear interest at 1% a month or fraction; interest under $5 is waived; a report, return or payment is deemed filed or paid on the date placed in the U.S. mail; a newly subject employer owes no penalty or interest if it files and pays within 10 days of the Department's notice; (i) a cash deposit or bond may be required after two delinquent quarters in four, and failing it adds a 2.0% surcharge; (k)(4) wage reports, contribution returns and payments due after June 30, 2024 must be filed and paid electronically by employers (and third-party administrators) with 25 or more employees, and the secretary may waive it for hardship.

sources.title: Kansas Administrative Regulations 50-2-3, Payment of contributions and benefit cost payments
sources.verifiedBy: fetched and read in full on 2026-11-12: (a) contributions are payable for each calendar quarter on wages paid in it; (b) a newly liable employer's first payment is due on or before the 25th day after the close of the quarter in which it becomes an employer; (f) when the regular payment day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday the payment is due the first regular business day after; (g) mail is deemed made on the postmark date; (i) late payments are subject to K.S.A. 44-717.

sources.title: Kansas Statutes 44-710 (employer contributions, payment; rates; reimbursing employers' reports and payments)
sources.revision: K.S.A. 44-710 as published by the Kansas Revisor of Statutes
sources.verifiedBy: fetched and read on 2026-11-12: (a) contributions are paid under the secretary's rules and are not deducted from employees' wages; no payment is required for a quarter's contributions under $5; reimbursing employers file quarterly wage reports by the last day of the month following the quarter, deemed filed when mailed.

sources.title: Kansas Department of Labor, Unemployment Tax (NASWA wage-file and payment-file specifications)
sources.verifiedBy: read: KDOL accepts the NASWA (ICESA) wage file as an ASCII .txt file of 275-character records, each line ended CR LF, with one Code A, one Code B, one or more Code E and one or more Code S records, a file name under 75 characters, and rejects an employer submitted twice in a quarter, future-quarter wage detail, an inactive account, total excess wages above total wages, or more than 99 employee records without an SSN; the payment file is ASCII of 381-character records in a zip, gz, bz2, txt or dat file of at most 5 MB (100 MB a day per organization). The field-by-field layouts were not in the text extracted.

efile.text: Kansas withholding tax reports must be filed and payment of tax made electronically.

deposits.interpretation: Kansas assigns one of five filing frequencies by the size of the employer's ANNUAL withholding (K.S.A. 79-3298): quad-monthly above $100,000.00; semi-monthly $8,000.01 to $100,000.00; monthly $1,200.01 to $8,000.00; quarterly $200.01 to $1,200.00; annually $200.00 or less. The initial frequency comes from the estimate on the business tax application, the Department reviews deposit history each year (notices mailed about November, effective January 1), and an employer must not file more or less often than assigned, so the frequency is an INPUT or is derived from a supplied annual liability. QUAD-MONTHLY: periods end on the 7th, 15th, 21st and last day, each due within three banking days. SEMI-MONTHLY: periods 1st-15th (due the 25th of the same month) and 16th-end (due the 10th of the next month). MONTHLY: due the 15th of the next month. QUARTERLY: due April 25, July 25, October 25 and January 25. ANNUAL: due January 25. A KW-5 is filed for every period even with no tax, and the director may require more frequent payments if money may be diverted. Due dates on a weekend or legal holiday move to the next regular business day. THIS IS THE OCTOBER 2024 EDITION.

returns.name: Form KW-5, Withholding Tax Deposit Report
contents: Filed with the payment for EACH reporting period even when no tax was withheld; annual filers still file a KW-5 for the year.
Electronically through the KDOR Customer Service Center; an amended or corrected KW-5 must be on paper.
Due dates follow the filing frequency (see the profile's deposit rules).

returns.name: Form KW-3, Annual Withholding Tax Return and Reconciliation
contents: Due by January 31 with the W-2s and 1099s that show Kansas withholding; must be filed electronically.
Reports the total Kansas tax withheld on W-2s and 1099s, credits, and the number of forms; all KW-5 payments for the year are entered.

Employers submitting more than 50 W-2 records must file them electronically; employers with fewer than 51 may send paper Copy 1 W-2s in Social Security number or alphabetical order with a copy of the electronic KW-3 submission (KW-100).

The Department's K-2MT Kansas W-2 Specifications for the Code RS (state) record, and the KCSC registration steps beyond the filing-frequency item.
The Department's power to require more frequent payment.

notModelled: Kansas legal holidays: K.A.R. 50-2-3(f) moves a payment day that falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday to the first regular business day after but does not list the legal holidays, and neither Kansas Department of Labor nor Department of Revenue page read publishes a list. The Governor's memorandum 'Designated Holidays for 2026' (2025-08-20; New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day observed Friday 2026-07-03, Labor Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and the Friday after, Christmas Eve and Christmas) was read, but it is a state employee holiday schedule, not the agencies' list, so it is not applied; due dates skip weekends only and carry the common warning. Kansas has no Presidents Day state holiday in that schedule.

returns.name: Quarterly wage report and unemployment tax return (K-CNS 100)
contents: Wage reports, contribution returns and contributions are due by the last day of the month following the quarter: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31. K.S.A. 44-717(a)(1) puts the penalty on a report or return not filed, and interest on contributions not paid, by that day.

A due date falling on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the first regular business day after (K.A.R. 50-2-3(f)); a report or payment is deemed made on the postmark date (K.A.R. 50-2-3(g), K.S.A. 44-717(a)(1)).

A newly liable employer's first payment is due on or before the 25th day after the close of the quarter in which it became an employer (K.A.R. 50-2-3(b)); it owes no penalty or interest if it files and pays within 10 days of the Department's notice that it is subject.

Employers and third-party administrators with 25 or more employees must file and pay electronically (K.S.A. 44-717(k)(4)), through the Employer Self Service Portal; the Department may waive it for hardship.

Taxable wage base $15,100 for 2026 ($15,700 for 2027); new employer rate 1.75% (5.55% for new construction employers); the rate range is 0% to 6.95% (HB 2570 Schedule C). Contributions are the employer's own and are not deducted from wages (K.S.A. 44-710(a)); a quarter's contributions under $5 need not be paid.

Late filing: .05% of the quarter's total wages for each month or fraction of a month, at least $25 and at most $200 per report. Late payment: interest of 1% a month or fraction; interest under $5 is waived (K.S.A. 44-717(a)(1)). A cash deposit or bond may be required after two delinquent quarters in four, and failing it adds a 2.0% surcharge (K.S.A. 44-717(i)).
Reimbursing employers file quarterly wage reports by the last day of the month following the quarter (K.S.A. 44-710).

notModelled: K.A.R. 50-2-3 states the 25th-day date only for a newly liable employer's first payment; the last-day-of-the-month date for a contributing employer's quarterly wage report, return and payment comes from K.S.A. 44-717(a)(1), which sets when the penalty and interest begin, not from a sentence that says 'due'.

The Department's FAQ is reported in a search result as saying employers with 26 or more employees must file online; K.S.A. 44-717(k)(4) says 25 or more, and the statute is used. The FAQ page itself was not in the text read.
The form number K-CNS 100 is taken from the Kansas Unemployment Insurance Employer Handbook as shown in a search result; the handbook was not read.
